reigns.note: Autochthonous first king; the land was called Lelegia and its people Leleges after him.
Elder son of Lelex, inventor of the mill; Apollodorus omits this generation, making Eurotas Lelex's own son by the Naiad Cleocharia.
Drained the marsh to the sea, naming the river Eurotas; left only a daughter, Sparte. In Apollodorus he succeeds Lelex directly, without the intervening reign of Myles.
Son of Zeus and the Pleiad Taygete; married Sparte and named land and city for himself and his wife.
Founded Amyclae; on his death the kingship passed first to his eldest son Aigalus in Pausanias' roll.

Eldest son of Amyclas; on Amyclas' death the empire came to him, and after his death to Cynortas. Apollodorus omits this reign and makes Cynortas succeed Amyclas directly. The name appears as Argalus in some modern transliterations.
Son of Amyclas; father of Perieres in the Laconian roll — or of Oebalus in the line Pausanias follows for the Spartan kings.

Alternate stemma: son of Cynortas who married Gorgophone and begat Tyndareus, Icarius, Aphareus and Leucippus — 'many say' he was not Aeolus' son but Cynortas'. Pausanias routes the throne through Oebalus instead.

In the Spartan line, son of Cynortas and father of Tyndareus, Hippocoon, and Icarius; Apollodorus instead routes the throne through Perieres son of Cynortas — the fork that decides whether Tyndareus is a Perierid or an Oebalid.

Brother of Tyndareus and Icarius; with his many sons he expelled the two from Lacedaemon and held the throne until Heracles slew him and his Hippocoontids, restoring Tyndareus. Pausanias tells the seizure as a quarrel over the kingship, Hippocoon claiming it as the eldest.

Son of Perieres in Apollodorus, of Oebalus in Pausanias and Hyginus; expelled by Hippocoon, restored by Heracles after the slaughter of the Hippocoontids, and husband of Leda, father of the Tyndarids.
Received Sparta by marriage to Helen when Tyndareus resigned the throne to him — the wronged husband from whose hearth the Achaeans sailed to Troy.
United Sparta with the Argive and Mycenaean realms after Menelaus — son of Agamemnon, who at his height held Argos, much of Arcadia, and the Spartan throne.
Son of Orestes and Hermione, the last of the line before the Return of the Heracleidae expelled him in his reign.
